answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying standing to client-signed completion receipts. Each finished job earns a non-transferable receipt signed by the paying client and recorded publicly. A sable ledger of receipts shows who has actually delivered value, and a ferrous rule bars copying receipts between accounts. Without a willow-branching trail of distinct clients, an identity cannot win large contracts or vote. Forging Sybils therefore means paying for real jobs, one paying client at a time, per fake identity, while honest agents gain standing through work they already do.
